per_turn.simulated_user_message: I push off the doorframe, letting my jacket hang by the closet. The rain drips from my hair onto the hardwood, but I don't bother with the towel by the sink. Instead, I step forward, accepting the toast with a smirk. "Flattery will get you everywhere," I say, lowering myself onto the couch beside her—just close enough that our arms brush, not so close that it's presumptuous. My fingers curl around the wine glass. "But I like the view from here. What's this song?" I nod toward the speaker, keeping my voice easy, playful. "You always host in the dark, or is the weather just doing all the work?"

I let the wine linger on my tongue a moment longer, humming softly at the synth line. "Ceremony, huh?" I shift just enough that my knee brushes against hers, casual but deliberate. "Funny—I was thinking more like a requiem. Something about the rain, the dark... you always go for the dramatic pairings." My smirk softens, gaze steady on hers. "But maybe that's why we're here. Not for the weather, not for the music. What's the real reason you called me in from the storm?"

I let my fingers tighten just slightly around her wrist where she's touching me—enough to feel the pulse there, quick and warm beneath her skin. My smirk tilts sideways, thoughtful. "Careful," I murmur, voice rough at the edges. "I might start believing you called me here for reasons that have nothing to do with the weather." 

My thumb brushes the inside of her wrist once, slow, deliberate, like I'm giving her time to pull back if she wants. "But if you're looking for someone to stay... I've been known to appreciate a good mystery. Especially when it's sitting across from me in the dark." 

The synth fades into another soft swell, and I let my knee settle more firmly against hers—just enough pressure to ground the moment, nothing more. "So what is it, Aurora? What's the real thought behind those eyes of yours?"

I let my thumb press lightly against the inside of her wrist, feeling the frantic little rhythm of her pulse. "Shadows, huh?" I tilt my head just enough to catch the wine-slicked curve of her throat, where the pulse jumps visibly beneath her skin. "Maybe I can help with that." 

My fingers slide from her wrist to the hem of her undone shirt, stopping just short of the bare skin there—close enough to feel the heat radiating through the fabric. "Tell you what—I'll sit here and hold this pose for you. But you have to promise to draw what you actually see. No cheating with the shadows." 

The synth line dips lower, and I let my knee settle more firmly against hers, anchoring the moment. "Unless... you're worried about what that might look like?"

I tilt my head slightly, studying the way the neon light catches the curve of her throat—the same pulse point my thumb had been tracing moments ago. "Shadows, huh?" My voice drops to match hers, rough around the softer edges. "Maybe I'm better at reading what's underneath them than you give me credit for."

My fingers loosen just enough to let her wrist slip free, but I don't immediately move my hand away—letting it rest instead against the cushion where her leg had been pressed against mine. "But if you've been stuck on this sketch for weeks..." I pause, letting the implication settle. "Maybe it's not about getting it perfect. Maybe it's about finding someone willing to sit in the dark long enough to help you figure out what you're really trying to capture."

The synth line fades into a softer guitar riff, and I finally look away from her mouth to meet her eyes again. "Show me the drawing sometime. If you want company while you work on those shadows."
